about: `node dist/node.js ops report --helper <version>` with the result file of the helper on stdin (store_result in scripts/ops-helper.sh). send_report looks for the text "ok":true or "ok":false in stdout. The first payload below is what the helper of 0.9.0 (still version 3) sends after an `access` request that turned remote access on; every key of its state is kept by the app. The third is a failed update that the helper took back after its self-test (after_update_check in scripts/lib/ops-selftest.sh): its state carries `watchdog` {at, from, to, reason}, which state_json adds from ops/watchdog.frag (watchdog_report in scripts/lib/ops-watchdog.sh). The app reads that key and does not keep it (parseWatchdog in services/ops-watchdog.ts: one ops_watchdog event and a notice to every admin for each `at`), so that case does not set keepsStateKeys.
